proof_summary: Assume the primes in question are bounded by \(M\), and apply positivity at \(n=M+3+2M^2\); for the resulting decomposition, \(x=\phi(p)\phi(q)\) satisfies \(x^4+1\le M\), hence \(x\le M\). Positivity of the totients, \(p=\phi(p)+1\), and the general estimate \(q\le 2\phi(q)^2\) then give \(p\le M+1\) and \(q\le2M^2\), contradicting the chosen value of \(n=p+q\).
